rooms.2800: A narrow office smelling of beeswax and old paper, with a broad desk scarred by decades of ink rings. Framed certificates hang crooked above a shelf of leather-bound registers, and a brass bell-pull dangles by the window. A single hard chair sits before the desk, polished smooth by nervous sitters. The only way out is the door east into the school's main hall.
rooms.2801: The great hall of the school house is a bustle of boots on scuffed boards, with the lesson bell hanging from a rope beside the stairs. Rows of pegs hold forgotten caps and satchels, and slates are stacked in leaning towers against the wall. Doors lead east to the janitor's office and west to the principal's, while the hallway runs on north past the classrooms. Stairs climb up to the floor above, and the entrance porch lies south.
rooms.2804: Chalk dust hangs in the air of this long hallway, drifting through slanting light from a high window. Pegs line the wall at child height, and a worn runner of rag carpet muffles little of the noise. A door east bears a small brass plate for the counselor, while an open doorway west shows a classroom. The hallway goes on north, and south it opens back into the main hall.
rooms.2807: Slates hang from nails along this stretch of hallway, each chalked with a name and a sum gone wrong. The floorboards are worn into a shallow groove down the middle by years of hurrying feet. East, a classroom door stands ajar, and west a plank door with a crescent cut in it leads out to the outhouse. A draught carries a whiff of lye soap from that way, and the hall continues north and south.
rooms.2810: Two doors face each other across the hallway here, one east and one west, both propped open with doorstops made from old iron weights. A tall cabinet against the wall holds rolled maps and a dented globe. The air is thick with the smell of ink and damp wool. Muddy bootprints cross the boards in all directions, and the hall continues north and south.
rooms.2813: The hallway smells of liniment and leather here, and a rack of wooden practice swords leans by the wall. Scuffed mats are stacked at the foot of the plaster beside a bucket of sand. A hand-painted sign on the west door announces the coach's office, while the classroom door east is plain oak. The hall goes on north toward the rear of the school and back south the way you came.
rooms.2816: The hallway ends in a heavy back door, rattling slightly in its frame, which opens north onto the yard behind the school. Cold air creeps beneath it and stirs the dust on the boards. To the west a wide arch gives onto the fencing hall, from which the clack of practice blades sometimes echoes. A coat of tarred canvas hangs stiff with old rain on a peg, and the hallway runs back south.
rooms.2817: A trampled yard lies behind the school house, bare of grass where generations of boots have packed it to hard earth. A scrubbed stone trough stands by the wall and a rain barrel gurgles under the eave. The timber back door leads south into the hallway, a cinder path leads on north to a covered track, and the stable's wide doors face east. Washing lines sag across the corner, hung with a few forgotten scarves.
rooms.2819: A dirt track runs beneath a long timber awning propped on rough posts, its beaten earth rutted by cartwheels. Rain-stained beams overhead drip faintly onto a row of upturned buckets. The covered way bends here, with the yard behind the school lying south and the track continuing east. A smell of hay and harness drifts along it.
rooms.2820: The covered track ends against the stable wall, its earth churned soft by hooves and scattered with strands of straw. Harness hooks stud the posts, each hung with a bridle gone stiff with age. The stable stands south through a wide arch, while the track runs back west. Light falls in dusty bars through gaps in the roof boards.
rooms.2818: The stable is a tall, dim barn of timber with stalls along either side, their half-doors gnawed at the top by bored teeth. Straw lies deep on the floor and a sweet smell of oats and leather fills the air. A saddle rack and a bucket of brushes sit by the entrance. The yard behind the school lies west through the wide doors, and a covered track leads north.
rooms.2815: A long, bare hall with a floor of pale boards chalked with lunge lines and the footwork of a hundred lessons. Wooden foils and padded jackets hang in tidy rows along a rack, and a tall mirror, flecked with age, throws back the light from the high windows. Prize ribbons droop from the rafters. An arch east leads back to the hallway, and a narrow door south opens on the coach's office.
rooms.2812: A cramped office cluttered with whistles, stopwatches and leather balls gone hard as stone. A battered desk is buried under rosters, and a cork board bristles with pinned team lists and faded ribbons. The place smells of boiled sweets and rubbing oil. A door north leads into the fencing hall, and another east opens on the hallway.
rooms.2814: Rows of sloped wooden desks fill this classroom, each with an inkwell and a carved groove for pens. A high stool stands before a slate board covered with the alphabet in careful copperplate. A string of picture cards runs along one wall, and a bucket of damp sponges waits beneath it. The only door opens west onto the hallway.
rooms.2809: Maps of coasts and kingdoms hang from rollers over the board of this classroom, their edges curling with age. A big painted globe stands on a tripod by the window, with one dent in its ocean where a careless elbow met it. A tin of coloured chalk, a rail of pointers and a table of salt-dough hills complete the room. The door west leads to the hallway.
rooms.2811: A sing-song classroom, with a tall wooden stand holding a tuning fork and a dented brass horn. Benches are arranged in tiers facing a lectern, and songsheets lie scattered across the boards in curling pages. The walls are hung with rhymes copied out in big, wobbly letters. A door east returns to the hallway.
rooms.2808: Beads strung on wooden frames stand along the sills of this counting room, and a tall abacus clacks gently in the draught. Sums in a looping hand cover the board, with one smudged correction in red. Stools stand in a ragged ring around a table piled with pebbles and tally sticks. The door west opens to the hallway.
rooms.2806: A narrow plank outhouse, leaning slightly, with a crescent moon cut high in the door and a draught whistling through the knots. A long bench with two holes sits above a bucket of lime, and squares of cloth hang on a nail. The graffiti of passing generations is scratched into the boards, much of it misspelled. The door opens east into the school hallway.
rooms.2803: A small, calm room where the noise of the school seems far away. Two soft chairs face each other over a faded rug, and a kettle sits on a little spirit stove beside a jar of honey. Shelves hold storybooks and a box of carved wooden animals, and a potted fern droops in the window. The door west leads out to the hallway.
rooms.2805: Neat rows of desks face a board ruled with lines for practising handwriting, each stroke looped and slanted just so. Quills stand in a jar on the teacher's table beside a pot of sand for blotting. Copybooks lie open on the desks, blotted and crossed out in a variety of styles. Light from a high window falls on a single door east, which leads to the hallway.
rooms.2802: A cluttered cupboard of a room smelling of lye, turpentine and wet rope. Mops hang from hooks, brooms lean in a bristly bunch, and a great ring of keys hangs on a nail above a bench littered with screws and tins of polish. A cot is folded against the wall under a shelf of oilcans. The only door leads west back to the main hall.
rooms.2832: The entrance porch is a draughty square of worn tiles with a boot scraper by the doorpost and a rack for wet cloaks. Heavy double doors stand open south onto the dirt track outside, and a notice board by them bristles with timetables and curling reminders. A brass handbell for visitors sits on a ledge. A door north leads into the main hall of the school.
rooms.2821: At the head of the stairs the upper hallway opens, its boards creaking at every step. A banister rubbed glossy by hands curves around the stairwell, which descends to the main hall below. East, a door carved with a laurel wreath marks the philosophy classroom, and the hallway runs on north. A skylight pours pale light over a long bench where latecomers wait.
rooms.2824: Sawdust drifts along the hallway from the workshop door west, and the sweet scent of cut pine mingles with chalk. A row of coat hooks carved into the shapes of acorns and owls lines the wall, clumsy and proud. East, a plain door opens on a classroom. The hallway continues north and back south.
rooms.2827: A tall window lets grey light fall across a mural of numbers painted along the wall, from one to a hundred, with tiny grinning faces drawn inside the zeros. West, a door with a brass plate showing a compass and set square opens on the mathematics classroom. The hallway runs on north toward more doors and back south.
rooms.2828: The hallway ends in a small landing where three doors meet. The door north has a chipped glass window and a smell of vinegar and burnt sulphur seeping through it, while east a faded timeline of kings is tacked to the frame of the history room. The west door stands plain beside a fire bucket, and the hallway leads back south.
rooms.2830: Benches scarred with acid burns run the length of this laboratory, crowded with stoppered jars of coloured salts and cloudy liquids. A brass microscope sits under a glass dome beside a tray of pressed ferns and a hanging prism that scatters rainbows over the ceiling. The air tastes faintly of sulphur. The only door leads south to the hallway.
rooms.2829: A long timeline is painted along the wall of this room, from cave paintings to the founding of the city, with dates scrawled beside it in chalk. A sand table holds a model of a siege, its toy walls toppled by many a reenactment. Cracked plaster busts of old rulers stare down from a shelf. The door west returns to the hallway.
rooms.2831: Easels and drawing boards crowd this bright classroom, and charcoal smudges every surface from the sills to the ceiling beams. A still life of apples, a jug and a tarnished candlestick sits on a stool, drawn a hundred times over. Pinned sketches curl on a line of string. The door east leads back to the hallway.
rooms.2826: Slate boards cover three walls of the mathematics classroom, packed with triangles, circles and long columns of figures. Wooden models of cones and cubes sit on the sills beside a pair of giant brass compasses. A chalk line has been drawn across the floor and labelled the equator, for reasons nobody remembers. The door east leads out to the hallway.
rooms.2823: A classroom for languages and speechmaking, with a raised lectern at one end and rows of benches facing it. Lists of foreign words are chalked in columns on the board, with their meanings left blank for the unwary. A small mirror hangs by the lectern so that a nervous speaker may watch their own face. The door west opens onto the hallway.
rooms.2825: The workshop is loud with the memory of mallets, and its floor is a drift of curled shavings. Workbenches carry vices, planes and chisels in neat racks, while half-built stools and toy boats wait on the shelves for glue to dry. A pot of hot resin sits over a tiny brazier. The only door leads east to the upstairs hallway.
rooms.2822: A bare, quiet room where the benches are set in a circle instead of rows. A single question is chalked on the board, with a scatter of arguments crossed out beneath it. Cushions have been worn flat by long thinking, and a sundial hangs oddly on the wall as if time were a puzzle too. The only door leads west to the hallway.
rooms.15201: Tall pillars of white marble flank the gate of Fameland, their capitals wreathed in carved laurel and gilded at the edges. A pair of bronze doors, green with age and sealed by a heavy bar, stand shut on the north, and beyond them lies a path no living foot has trodden in years. East, a door leads back to the Temple Library, while the hall continues west beneath a vaulted ceiling. Braziers of white fire burn in niches on either side.
rooms.15202: A long gallery of polished marble stretches ahead, its floor so smooth that the flames of the wall braziers shine twice over. Alcoves in the walls hold statues of armoured figures, each plinth bearing a name in gold leaf. The air is cool and still and tastes faintly of incense. The gate lies east, and the gallery runs on west.
rooms.15203: Three halls meet here on a floor inlaid with a great golden compass rose set in black and white stone. A tall statue of a hero with a raised sword stands at the centre, his shadow thrown long by the surrounding braziers. Pale banners hang from the vault, their embroidered devices faded past reading. The gallery leads east back toward the gate, one hall runs north into splendour, and another south toward quieter chambers.
rooms.15204: The Halls of Victory begin with a broad avenue of red-veined marble, lined by pairs of bronze pillars crowned with laurel. Captured standards hang from the walls in long, stiff folds, their poles crossed over painted shields. A drum the height of a man rests on a stone plinth bearing the date of some forgotten triumph. The hall runs on north, and back south it meets the great crossing.
rooms.15205: Here the hall turns, and a magnificent trophy wall rises to the roof, hung with broken spears, dented helms and the blades of defeated enemies. Beneath each trophy a small marble plaque records the battle where it was won. Torches in golden sconces burn with a steady flame that gives no smoke. The hall leads south toward the crossing and bends west.
rooms.15206: A long corridor stands lined on both sides with carved panels depicting charge, siege and rout in fine marble relief. Wreaths of bronze laurel have been fixed above every door frame, gone black with age. The faint smell of old oil and polished stone lingers, and somewhere a sound like distant trumpets seems to fade as you listen. The hall continues east and west.
rooms.15207: The victory halls end in a chamber with a vaulted ceiling painted with a golden sunrise over a field of banners. Beneath it a marble plinth holds a laurel crown cast in bronze, set before a carved roll listing the victors by rank. The air is cold enough to raise a shiver. The hall runs back east, and a dark archway leads south into the Chamber of the Fallen Ones.
rooms.15210: A round chamber of grey stone, hushed and solemn, with a cenotaph of black marble at its heart. Names of the fallen are carved up the walls in tight rows, some freshly cut and some worn almost smooth. Candles in iron holders gutter though no draught stirs. Archways open east and west into smaller niches, the way north returns to the victory halls, and a passage runs south into the Chambers of Sorrow.
rooms.15209: A small stone alcove, its walls hung with torn pennants of regiments long disbanded. A bench of cold marble faces a carved roll where each name has a single date beside it. A bowl of white sand holds a few burnt-down incense sticks left by earlier visitors. The only way out is the archway west into the chamber.
rooms.15212: Soft grey light seeps from lamps behind frosted glass, falling on walls inscribed with laments in flowing letters. Marble weeping figures kneel in niches, their faces veiled in carved cloth. The chamber is cold and its echo is strange, as if it answered a few moments late. The Chamber of the Fallen Ones lies north, the passage runs south, and an arch opens west.
rooms.15213: A narrow passage of dark stone, its floor worn into two shallow channels by the passage of mourners. Black ribbons hang from iron hooks along the walls, brittle with age and rustling faintly. Each hook has a name stamped on a tiny brass tag, though many have gone green and are unreadable. The passage runs north and south.
rooms.15214: A slow bend in the passage, with a low alcove cut into the wall where a lamp burns before a stone urn. Dry petals lie scattered around its base, still faintly fragrant after years. The walls are lined with rows of little tablets, each carved with a single word of farewell. The passage goes back north and turns west.
rooms.15215: Four passages meet here beneath a low dome whose underside is painted with a night sky of silver stars. A fountain with no water in it stands in the middle, its basin filled with white pebbles left by mourners. Faint singing from nowhere seems to drift through the stone. Ways lead north to a small chamber, east into the Chambers of Sorrow, south toward the corridors, and west into the Halls of Eternity.
rooms.15216: A small, bare chamber with a single stone bench and a candle in a niche, kept for those who wish to grieve alone. The walls are plain except for a narrow band of carved lilies running around at shoulder height. The silence is deep enough to hear your own breath. The doorways lead north and south.
rooms.15217: The passage widens into a hall of tall pillars, each carved with the figure of a mourning woman holding a lamp. A lintel above the arch is inscribed with the words of a lament that fade into the stone as you read. Cold air breathes in from the way west, and the dust on the floor lies undisturbed. A door leads east, an archway leads south into a little chamber, and the hall opens west into the Halls of Eternity.
rooms.15233: The Halls of Eternity begin in a long hall of dark green marble, polished until it mirrors the braziers that never go out. Rows of statues stand along the walls, each with a plaque naming its deeds in letters of gold. The air hums faintly, like a held note. The hall opens east into the Chambers of Sorrow and turns south.
rooms.15234: Three wide ways meet in a small court of pale stone, where a single flame burns in a bronze bowl on a pedestal. Its light throws the shadows of the surrounding statues long across the floor, so that they appear to lean toward you. A scroll of beaten gold hangs on the wall, listing those who kept faith. The halls lead north, south and west.
rooms.15235: A short hall of white marble ends at a wall where a vast mosaic shows a procession of heroes climbing toward a golden door. The tiles glitter in the light of two tall braziers that have burned since before anyone's grandfather. A bench of polished stone invites you to rest, though the stone is cold as a river. The hall runs north, and an archway leads east into the Chambers of Sorrow.
rooms.15236: The hall turns a corner here between two great pillars wrapped in carved ivy and bearing the names of heroes at their feet. A banner of deep blue silk, embroidered with a silver star, hangs from an iron pole and stirs though the air is still. The flagstones are worn pale along the centre by pilgrims' feet. The hall leads east toward the court and south along a gallery.
rooms.15237: A straight gallery of dark stone, with statues standing on either side like soldiers on parade. Each wears a different harness and holds a different weapon, but all have the same calm, unseeing eyes. Their plaques bear dates in ancient numerals, and a thin layer of dust lies over everything but the floor. The gallery runs north and south.
rooms.15238: Gilded honour rolls fill the walls of this stretch of the hall, line upon line of names with the title and deed set beside each. A brazier on a tripod burns at either end, the flames white and steady, unflickering in any breath. The cold seems to gather around the lowest panels, where the newest names have been cut. The gallery goes north and south.
rooms.15239: The gallery bends beside a tall window of coloured glass, which throws crimson and gold across the marble. Beneath it a stone trough holds a heap of withered garlands laid by mourners long gone. A line of small bronze lamps burns along the sill, each marked with a name. The hall leads back north and goes on east.
rooms.15240: A broad vaulted passage, its ceiling painted midnight blue and spangled with golden stars. Trophies of old campaigns fill the wall niches: a cracked drum, a bent trumpet, a captain's helm with its plume rotted away. The floor is inlaid with a long strip of laurel leaves in green stone. The passage runs east and west.
rooms.15241: The hall ends in a pair of high pillars crowned with winged victories of bronze, their wings dark with age. Between them a floor of black and white squares leads on like a great game board. A faint scent of lilies hangs in the air, though no flower grows in this place. The way leads west back along the hall, and east into the corridors.
rooms.15219: A narrow corridor of grey stone runs along a wall of memorial tablets, each carved with a name and a line of remembrance. Small lamps burn beneath them, and many have been replenished with fresh oil. The passage forks here, one way leading north, another west to the Halls of Eternity, and a broad arch opening east into the Chambers of Heroes.
rooms.15218: A plain corridor with a low ceiling, kept dim so that the letters on the walls gleam in the little light there is. Rows of oblong plaques commemorate the dead of some old war, and their names are arranged by company. A bench is set into the wall for those who wish to read slowly. The corridor leads north to the Chambers of Sorrow and south to a junction.
rooms.15220: Here the chambers of the heroes begin, a great high-roofed hall lined with life-sized bronze statues on stone pedestals. Each hero is shown in the pose of a famous moment, sword drawn or banner raised or hand reaching out to a fallen friend. A banner of yellow silk hangs above the doorway, bordered with gold fringes. The hall runs north and south, and an arch leads west to the corridors.
rooms.15227: Marble statues of four heroes stand shoulder to shoulder in this corner of the hall, their cloaks carved so fine they seem to ripple. At their feet lies a stone shield, scored by the blows of a real fight, set into the floor as a memorial. The braziers at either end give a light like melted amber. The hall turns here, running east and back south.
rooms.15226: A wide avenue of statues stretches through the chamber, set in pairs facing each other across the polished floor. Each pair is a champion and the foe who nearly bested them, carved with equal respect. A wall of honour plaques runs behind them, spaced with painted heraldry. The hall runs east and west.
rooms.15225: The statues give way to a wall of hanging shields, hundreds of them, each painted with the device of a family or order. Some are cracked, some gilded, and some covered with a black cloth where the house has died out. A low rail in front keeps the curious from touching. The chamber turns here, with a doorway south into the Room of Mercy and the hall going west.
rooms.15224: The Room of Mercy is round and white-walled, lit by a high oculus that casts a pillar of cold light on a stone altar. Offerings of ribbons, coins and small carved charms lie on its surface. A bronze bowl for tears stands beside it, polished by many hands. Doorways lead north, east and south.
rooms.15228: A small, serene chamber where the walls are covered in soft grey drapery and the floor is strewn with rushes. A carved bench runs round three sides beneath a frieze of open hands. The flames in the brazier are low and bluish, giving a hush to the room. The room opens north and west.
rooms.15229: Pale marble in the shape of a kneeling figure fills an alcove in this room, one hand outstretched in forgiveness. Candle stubs gather in a heap around its base, melted into fantastic shapes. A heavy oak door east is bound with brass and marked with a wreath. The passage runs north and back south.
rooms.15230: Doors in three directions open from this crossing of the Halls of Mercy, each framed by an arch of pale stone and a polished brass plate. The floor is laid with a mosaic of a dove carrying an olive branch, its colours kept fresh by regular scrubbing. A faint draught flutters the candle flames. Ways lead north and south, and doors lead east and west into honour rooms.
rooms.15231: The passage ends in a dead-end hall with a high ceiling hung with paper lanterns, each inscribed with a wish for the departed. They sway slightly, though nothing moves the air. A heavy wooden door to the east is carved with a laurel wreath. The hall leads back south, and an archway opens west into the Room of Mercy.
rooms.15243: A small private shrine for a single hero, its walls hung with a tapestry of a battlefield at dawn. A stone sarcophagus stands in the centre, the lid carved with a recumbent figure with hands crossed on a sword. Eternal candles burn in four brass stands around it. The only way out is the door west.
rooms.15232: A quiet, shadowed hall of tall narrow windows set with milky glass, through which comes a soft diffused light. A long rug of faded rose leads between two rows of benches, towards a lectern. The walls are bare except for a single plaque reading a verse on kindness. The hall runs north to the crossing and east toward the Halls of Mercy.
rooms.15244: This honour room is a low vault, its walls lined with niches that each hold a small bronze urn and a palm leaf of carved stone. A single lamp burns in the middle of the floor, on a pedestal wrapped in brass vines. The names on the urns are in an old tongue, and the air smells of cedar. The door west leads back to the Halls of Mercy.
rooms.15242: Banners of a vanished kingdom hang here in fading ranks, their crowns and lions barely visible. A marble table holds a book of names bound in black leather, chained to its stand and open to a page with a ribbon. The room is bitterly cold, as if winter had settled in the corners. The only door leads east.
rooms.15245: A grander honour room, its walls panelled in dark wood and hung with portraits of heroes in oils, their eyes dark and attentive. Crossed swords are mounted over a stone fireplace in which no fire has been laid for generations. Velvet chairs stand around a table set with a goblet of dry dust. The heavy door leads west.
rooms.15223: The hall opens into a splendid chamber whose floor is inlaid with an immense laurel wreath in gold. Statues in the niches around it hold lamps aloft, giving a warm, steady light. A plaque at the entrance names the fallen who held this very spot. A doorway north leads to the Room of Mercy, and the way continues west toward a famous road.
rooms.15222: This is the Way of Heroes itself, a broad processional road of white stone between rows of pillars, each pillar topped by a statue facing the way. Gold leaf runs in the grooves of the paving, worn thin by centuries of walking. A deep, ceremonial hush lies over everything. The way leads east into a chamber and west into another.
rooms.15221: The corner of the Chambers of Heroes is dominated by a colossal statue of a woman in plate, her visor raised and her sword planted before her like a cross. Fresh lamps burn at her feet in a ring, and the floor around her is polished by kneeling. Her carved eyes seem to follow whoever approaches. A passage runs north, and the way east leads to the Way of Heroes.
rooms.15211: A narrow alcove, tucked away from the grand chamber, where a single stone sarcophagus has been set into the wall. The inscription on its face is half rubbed away, as if many hands had touched it. A small lamp with a flame the colour of pearl burns on a ledge. The only way out is east, back into the Chamber of the Fallen Ones.
